Name: Obadiah
Summary: Obadiah is the shortest book of the Old Testament: a single-chapter prophecy against Edom, probably delivered around or after Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC (the exact date is debated). He condemned Edom for standing by — and joining in — when Babylon plundered Judah, and promised that the kingdom shall be the LORD's.
KeyStory: Obadiah pronounced judgment on Edom for its pride and its violence against brother Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's calamity.
LifeLesson: Pride falls hardest when it feeds on a brother's suffering. Do not rejoice over another's calamity — the day of the LORD comes to all nations alike.
